reasoning: The FHA count (Count 6) survived the motion to dismiss; only the negligence per se counts (3 and 4) predicated on the FHA were dismissed. The disability-related FHA claim itself was not dismissed at the pleading stage.
Third-party motion to dismiss denied; plaintiff's FHA disability claim survived the pleading stage. This appears to be a misfilter into the defendant-win/procedural pool.
Section 1915 screening dismissed pro se complaint alleging neighbor disputes with no cognizable FHA theory; facts do not map to any FHA cause of action.
Court dismissed FHA claim because allegations were conclusory labels without facts tying disability to any adverse housing action.

source_file: 10338845_2025_Lee v. Omaha Housing Authority Foundation Inc._ned
reasoning: FHA claim dismissed because plaintiff alleged no facts on protected-class membership or a causal link between protected activity and adverse housing action.

reasoning: Pro se conclusory allegations dismissed; no facts showing defendant's notice of disability or similarly situated comparators tied to the FHA elements.
FHA claim dismissed as time-barred under the two-year statute of limitations.

FHA retaliation claim against HUD employee barred by sovereign immunity; court disposed on jurisdictional grounds without reaching merits.

source_file: 10769944_2026_James B. Herrera v. Maddox Management, LLC_nmd
reasoning: Disability allegation conclusory; causation/elements not tied to specific pleaded facts about defendant's conduct.
FHAA claim dismissed on threadbare allegations; elements recited but not tied to specific pleaded facts.
FHA/ADA damages claim dismissed because plaintiff did not allege disparate treatment connecting the adverse action to protected-class membership; elements of disparate treatment not matched to facts.
Plaintiffs were landlords, not a protected class of persons with disabilities; no cognizable FHA theory available given pleaded posture.
Court held plaintiff 'sufficiently stated a claim' under the FHA; claim survived the motion to dismiss, indicating upstream misfilter.
SAC dismissed for lack of Article III injury-in-fact; court did not reach FHA merits because plaintiffs failed to plead facts showing personal injury.

FHA familial-status count dismissed because plaintiff, a single homeless male with no minor children, did not fit the statutory definition of 'familial status'; facts do not match the invoked theory's technical element.
Court expressly faulted plaintiff for failing to allege the city turned off water because of her disability or that landlord took advantage of her disability; no causal link pled.
Motion to dismiss for failure to prosecute was DENIED; no pleading-stage failure occurred. This is an upstream misfilter.
FHA refusal-to-rent/failure-to-accommodate claim dismissed as barred by the two-year FHA statute of limitations; equitable tolling and continuing-violation arguments rejected.
Motions to dismiss administratively denied as moot; plaintiff granted leave to amend before any substantive dismissal of the FHA claim.

FHA disability-discrimination claim dismissed because plaintiff alleged husband's alcoholism as handicap but failed to tie any defendant action to that disability; elements stated but not connected to facts.

Court held plaintiff alleged discrimination based on gender identity but did not allege a disability under the FHAA or tie defendants' conduct to a cognizable FHA protected status; disability nexus missing.
